summary: Sega's Dinosaur King began as a 2005 collectible-card arcade game and later expanded into a Nintendo DS RPG, anime, manga, and card-game merchandise.

entries.title: Dinosaur King
entries.definitive_edition: Original Sega arcade cabinet/card route, with DS version documented separately

emulation.notes: Original cabinet/card capture is preferred. DS emulation is only for the handheld adaptation if legally sourced.
emulation.fidelity_ceiling: Working arcade cabinet with physical cards and scanner behavior documented

primary.version: Original Sega card-dispensing arcade cabinet with cards
primary.why: The original Dinosaur King is a card-based Sega arcade game, so the correct archive target is cabinet behavior, scanner/card state, and physical-card availability. The Nintendo DS game is related and more accessible, but it is a different RPG adaptation.
primary.how_to_play: Use an original cabinet or verified arcade setup with legitimate cards where possible. Record cabinet/version/region, card set, scanner/card condition, dinosaur/move cards, battle mode, opponent, language, service settings, and whether the DS game was sampled separately.

secondary.exclusive_content: Story/RPG adaptation with dinosaur collection and Wi-Fi-era features
secondary.what_to_play: Use as the practical home-version comparison route.
secondary.why: It is not a substitute for the card-scanning arcade cabinet.

all_releases.reason: primary: origin route and physical-card/scanner target.
secondary: accessible home-version comparison, not the arcade target.

fidelity_vs_completeness_conflict.note: The arcade cabinet/card route and DS RPG adaptation are different games/routes.

entries.remaster_caveats: Availability is preservation-dependent; record card/cabinet provenance and do not rely on unofficial dumps as the primary route.
